from common import *

import numpy as np
import random

# concepts:
# grid-splitting, row-detection, color-0

# description:
# Split the grid into separate sections at each full row of color-0 (black),
# ensuring each resulting section is exactly two rows tall.
# If there are odd rows between splits, the last section will have only one row.

def main(input_grid):
    # List to hold the sections of the grid
    sections = []

    # Initialize the start index for the first section
    start_idx = 0

    # Iterate over each row in the grid
    for idx in range(input_grid.shape[0]):
        # Check if the current row is fully filled with color-0 (black)
        if np.all(input_grid[idx, :] == Color.BLACK):
            # If there are rows between start_idx and current idx, split the grid
            if idx > start_idx:
                section = input_grid[start_idx:idx, :]
                # If the section is odd in height, add an extra row to make it even
                if section.shape[0] % 2 != 0:
                    section = np.vstack([section, np.zeros((1, section.shape[1]), dtype=int)])
                sections.append(section)
            # Update the start index to the row after the current black row
            start_idx = idx + 1

    # Add the last section if it exists
    if start_idx < input_grid.shape[0]:
        section = input_grid[start_idx:, :]
        # If the section is odd in height, add an extra row to make it even
        if section.shape[0] % 2 != 0:
            section = np.vstack([section, np.zeros((1, section.shape[1]), dtype=int)])
        sections.append(section)

    # Create the output grid by stacking sections vertically
    output_grid = np.vstack(sections) if sections else np.array([], dtype=int)

    return output_grid

def generate_input():
    # Randomly determine the size of the grid
    n_rows = random.randint(10, 20)
    n_cols = random.randint(5, 10)

    # Initialize the grid with random colors that are not black
    grid = np.random.choice(list(Color.NOT_BLACK), size=(n_rows, n_cols))

    # Randomly place full rows of color-0 (black) in the grid
    num_black_rows = random.randint(1, 3)
    black_row_indices = randomly_spaced_indices(n_rows, num_black_rows, border_size=1, padding=2)

    for idx in black_row_indices:
        grid[idx, :] = Color.BLACK

    return grid
